clue.text: Survive predicted widespread storms, possibly

blocks.note: to weather a crisis is to come through it
forecast is a past form of the verb meaning to predict

explanation.surface: Someone vows to come through the storms that were predicted to sweep the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Survive predicted' reads as a phrase about enduring a prophecy; it is two separate synonyms placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin saying storms will be widespread is an example of what a meteorologist issues, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Act corruptly in Nato for the present

indicators.note: something done corruptly is bent out of its proper shape, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: to do is to act
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone is behaving dishonestly within NATO for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the present' reads as 'for now'; 'present' is the definition, a noun meaning gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift of money or goods, which is a present in the noun sense.

clue.text: Blows very loudly during encore

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: bis is a call for a repeat performance, like 'encore'
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A trumpeter plays at full blast while giving an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical setting of the surface hides that 'Blows' means punches, not blowing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A biff is an informal word for a punch, so biffs are blows struck with a fist.

clue.text: Account in which one acted badly

indicators.note: acting badly means the performance is garbled, so the preceding letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A story told by someone about the time they gave a poor performance on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short story or account of an incident, usually a personal one.

clue.text: Sympathy recedes after extremely foul dump

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are used
something receding goes backwards, so the word for sympathy is written in the opposite direction
this places the word for sympathy behind the other piece in the answer

blocks.note: the first and last letters of foul
pity is sympathy, here written backwards

explanation.surface: Pity ebbs away on seeing a filthy rubbish tip.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, fly-tipping means dumping rubbish illegally, by a roadside or in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly-tip is to discard waste illegally, so it is a specific way to dump rubbish.

clue.text: Resolved cases receive overdue increases

indicators.note: something resolved has been broken down and settled anew, so the following letters are rearranged
to receive something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged
overdue means late

explanation.surface: Once legal cases are settled, people get pay rises that were long overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as 'settled' in the legal surface, but it means the letters are sorted out afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to grow or intensify, so escalates matches increases as a verb.

clue.text: Take action to support quiet closure of caribou reindeer hunt

indicators.note: the closure of a word is where it ends, so the final letters of the following words are taken
in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so the legal action comes last

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
the last letters of each word
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Campaigners go to court to back a quiet halt to hunting caribou and reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hunt' seems to belong with the animals in the surface, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue is to chase after something, which is what it means to hunt quarry.

clue.text: Initially speak about my poor friend with feeling

indicators.note: initially points at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
turned about means facing the other way, so the next word runs backwards

blocks.note: first letter of speak
my written backwards
poor in the sense of feeble or inadequate
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone begins talking warmly about an unfortunate friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'concerning' in the surface, but it turns the next word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sympathetically means showing compassion, that is, acting with feeling for another's troubles.

clue.text: Switch to email on moving

indicators.note: to switch things around is to change their positions, so the following letters are reordered

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to change over to email while relocating offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like house-moving in the surface; it is the definition, meaning touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moving stirs the feelings, which is what an emotional scene or speech does.

clue.text: State imprisons upper-class Tory as impudent

indicators.note: to imprison something is to lock it inside, so the other letters go within the first word

blocks.note: to state is to say
U is the standard abbreviation for upper-class
C stands for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: The government jails a posh Conservative for cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY holds U and C. Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucy describes cheeky, disrespectful behaviour, a close synonym of impudent.

clue.text: Trade tariff wrongly calculated at the outset

indicators.note: something done wrongly is out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the outset is the very start, so just the first letter of the preceding word is taken

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
first letter of calculated

explanation.surface: A trade levy got its sums wrong right from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to deal or trade, often in illicit goods, and as a noun it means commerce.

clue.text: Pasteur beaten to shreds

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the scientist's name, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The great microbiologist is soundly defeated, torn to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shreds' reads as one phrase, but 'to' is just the link and 'shreds' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred paper is to rip it into strips, which is exactly what someone who tears it up does.

clue.text: Awesome digital image?

blocks.note: first meaning: tremendous, in the slang sense
second meaning: an electronic picture, split as e- plus a short word for picture

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a playful split: E for electronic, as in email, and PIC for picture. The question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic is current slang for impressive or amazing, and an e-pic is an electronic photograph.

clue.text: Too satisfied with firm's first Manchester location not being empty

indicators.note: first marks the beginning, so only the opening letter of the city name is used
a word that is empty has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
first letter of Manchester
a location is a place
the outer letters of not

explanation.surface: A company smug about its first Manchester premises not standing vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm's first' looks like it should give F; 'first' belongs to Manchester, and 'firm's' is CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Complacent describes someone smugly content and uncritical, satisfied to an excessive degree.

clue.text: Leap in cab awkwardly, helplessly drunk

indicators.note: doing something awkwardly means clumsily, so the preceding letters land in a muddled order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reveller stumbles clumsily into a taxi after one too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk and incapable' is a British legal charge, so incapable alone can mean too drunk to function.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapable, in the phrase drunk and incapable, means so intoxicated as to be unable to look after oneself.

clue.text: Acceptable to frame African politicians for money

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the first word encloses the next piece

blocks.note: fine means acceptable or all right
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's ruling party

explanation.surface: It is deemed acceptable to fit up African politicians in exchange for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' suggests a false accusation in the surface; here it means to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means funds or money, especially the money needed for a project.

clue.text: Break the French after Western struggle

indicators.note: after places the first two pieces behind the abbreviation for the direction

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for Western
a rest is a break
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A break for the French following a Western struggle, like a pause in a historical conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple or fight, which is a physical struggle.

clue.text: Current drop in unexpected income

blocks.note: wind is a current of air
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: A financial report notes a present slump in surprise earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as 'present-day' but is a noun, a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is a sudden piece of good fortune, especially money one did not expect to receive.

clue.text: Pass on characteristic involving, primarily, nose, skull and mouth

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the word for characteristic wraps round the other letters
primarily means first of all, so the initial letter of each following word is used

blocks.note: a trait is a characteristic
the first letters of nose, skull and mouth

explanation.surface: An inherited facial feature handed down to the next generation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' belongs to the list of features, not a letter source; only the three nouns are initialled.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to send or convey, so passing on a message or disease is transmitting it.

clue.text: Getting back to being on the dole again?

blocks.note: first meaning: recovering something one had lost
second meaning, split as re- plus a word for drawing benefits: claiming once more

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cryptic: 'claiming' is British slang for drawing unemployment benefit, the dole, and the prefix re- makes it happen again; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to recover possession of something, and re-claiming is literally making a benefit claim once more.

clue.text: Worry about overturning progress

indicators.note: something overturned is upended, so in this down clue the short word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: care is anxiety or worry
re, Latin for concerning, turned upside down

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a reversal will undo their advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is read as RE, the usual crossword shorthand for regarding, before it is flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is a person's progress through working life, the course of advancement in a profession.

clue.text: Threat makes people join a church

indicators.note: joining puts things side by side, so the pieces are set down one after another

blocks.note: men are people
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A worrying congregation trend: people signing up to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a danger or source of threat, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Appears in what's a risqué garment

indicators.note: something that appears in a phrase is sitting inside its letters, spanning the word breaks

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone shows up wearing something slightly racy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a long draped garment worn chiefly by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Time to let up being a wind-up merchant

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ease is to let up or slacken

explanation.surface: A plea for a prankster to stop and give everyone a break.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a wind-up merchant is someone who habitually provokes people for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tease is a person who mocks or provokes others playfully, just like a habitual joker.

clue.text: Could be dead start to afternoon at home for sure

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken from the following word

blocks.note: a cert, short for certainty, is often called a dead cert
first letter of afternoon
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone at home in the early afternoon is surely dead, as in a whodunnit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be dead' defines by example: the word is one that 'dead' often qualifies, as in the British phrase a dead cert, a sure winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain means definite or assured, so it can replace the adverbial phrase for sure.

clue.text: Delivers lilac regularly as a flower

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the colour word is taken

blocks.note: to deliver is to set free
the second and fourth letters of lilac

explanation.surface: A florist's van regularly brings lilac blooms around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivers' suggests the florist's van, but it is meant in the sense of rescuing.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant flowering plant from southern Africa, popular in bouquets.

clue.text: Take wickets finally with a duck

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the previous word is kept

blocks.note: last letter of wickets
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A bowler takes wickets at last, after a batter is out for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to take something that is not yours, so take works as a synonym.

clue.text: Divine girl ensnares established lecturer

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap something within, so the name wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: a girl's name
est. is the abbreviation for established
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A gorgeous young woman catches a long-serving academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as describing the girl but is the definition; the lecturer's letter is added after the trapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means heavenly, belonging to the sky or the realm of the gods, so it matches divine.
